critical_passages.evidence: Explicitly asserts upper semicontinuous inv, nu, rho independently. The source assertion itself does not cure the branch-formula counterexample.
Contained boundary strata and isolated codimension-one support components receive inv=(s,infinity,0,...), nu=0, rho=empty.
Ambient primary invariant prepends boundary count; nu and rho are inherited from the lower-dimensional restricted ideal.

On companion support the primary invariant prepends residual order divided by marking; auxiliary invariants are copied from the companion. Successive assignment transfers values through unchanged points.
Monomial branch has constant primary zero, nu=ord(M)/mu and rho selected by inclusion-minimal threshold subsets. Chart exceptional exponent is sum_A(a)-mu<a_j.

Functoriality, embedding prefixes and semilinear transport depend on equality of the branch data and invariant values. Galois descent uses canonical centers. Separate auxiliary semicontinuity is unnecessary to these comparisons.
Modified mark-one monomial branch has primary priority 3/2 and uses monomial nu/rho on that primary stratum. Pair semicontinuity is compatible with this construction.

confirmed_objection.input: X=A^2_K, I=(x(x+y)), mu=1, E={V(x)}; K algebraically closed of characteristic zero
confirmed_objection.calculation: M=(x), N=(x+y). Along V(x) minus the origin residual order is zero, so the monomial branch assigns primary zero, nu=1, rho={V(x)}. At the origin residual order is one; the companion (x+y,1) restricts in Step 1a to (y,1) on V(x), with empty restricted boundary. Its codimension-one branch assigns nu=0 and rho=empty. The origin primary is (1,1,1,0,infinity,0,...) in unencoded source coordinates and is strictly greater than primary zero.
confirmed_objection.failure: The standalone loci {nu>=1} and {rho>empty} are V(x) minus the origin, not closed in support V(x) union V(x+y). Both original Definition(ii) and Proposition(1) overstate the displayed construction.
confirmed_objection.logical_limit: This refutes standalone semicontinuity of the stated branch functions, not the abstract possibility of different auxiliary functions satisfying an existential theorem.

recommended_interface.decision: Retain the source algorithm, its exact invariant values, rational encoding, center priority, pointwise descent, termination and functoriality. Correct independent auxiliary semicontinuity to lexicographic pair semicontinuity.
recommended_interface.definition_ii_exact_replacement: (ii) inv has finite range on each support and is upper semicontinuous there; the lexicographically ordered pairs (inv,nu) and (inv,rho) are also upper semicontinuous. Equivalently, nu and rho are upper semicontinuous on each level stratum {inv=a}.
recommended_interface.nu_range_addendum: The construction also gives finite ranges for nu and rho on each stage support. The definition may state this as well; rho is automatically finite because E_i is finite.
recommended_interface.proposition_1_exact_replacement: (1) there are successively defined invariants inv, nu and rho with the existing codomains and finite ranges on each support; inv and the lexicographic pairs (inv,nu), (inv,rho) are upper semicontinuous, equivalently the auxiliary functions are upper semicontinuous on each fixed-inv stratum.

proof_repairs.repair: After owner adjudication and completed proof edits, remove the opening not-supplied caveat, set proof provenance to ai-altered, and replace the final unresolved-claim remark with the explicit counterexample explaining the corrected interface. Do not mark supplied before proof and consumers are integrated.

Keep branchwise primary USC but replace any assertion that the fixed-leading-coordinate stratum is closed with a finite-range level-stratum closure argument. Such strata are locally closed, not generally closed.

Prove nu and rho USC on each fixed-primary level stratum. In terminal infinity branches they are constant zero/empty. In monomial branches, nu is a finite sum of nonnegative boundary exponents divided by the mark, and rho superlevels are finite unions of boundary intersections indexed by eligible threshold subsets. In boundary or hypersurface reductions a fixed ambient primary tuple fixes both the leading coordinate and the entire lower-dimensional primary tail, so the induction hypothesis applies to the corresponding lower-primary level stratum. Maximal boundary pieces are disjoint on the relevant support; maximal-contact charts agree etale-locally; unchanged-lift transfer transports these relative-closed loci to earlier stages.

State why inv and nu ranges are finite on each support: finite-type Noetherian ambient gives finitely many components/charts; only finitely many pass-start residual orders, boundary counts, monomial exponents and marks occur in each terminating recursive construction; each dimension reduction lowers dimension, so the tuple has uniformly bounded depth; each finite collection of lower-dimensional stage invariants has finite range by induction. E_i is finite, hence rho has finite range. This justifies level strata and maximum attainment; an infinite padded tail adds no new values.

For f=inv with finite range, fix a attained value a and S_a={f=a}. Since {f>a} is a finite union of closed superlevels, S_a is locally closed in {f>=a}. If F={x in S_a:g(x)>=b} is closed in S_a, then closure(F) lies in {f>=a} and closure(F) intersect S_a=F. Thus closure(F) is contained in F union {f>a}, and {f>a} union F is closed. This set is the superlevel of (f,g) at (a,b). If a is unattained, it is simply {f>a}, again closed. Apply to g=nu and g=rho. This establishes full lex-pair USC from the stated stratum induction without using false standalone USC.

Make the already valid pointwise estimate explicit: at q mapping to p in the chosen center, choose a chart j in its minimal threshold subset A. Put b=sum_{D in A}a_D-mu<a_j. Every surviving old strict divisor through q lies over an old divisor through p, so ord_q(M_new)<=b+sum_{D through p,D!=j}a_D<ord_p(M_old). Divisors absent at q only reduce the sum. Hence nu strictly drops at every surviving support point above the center, including Cartier-center blowups, not just at generic points of replacement components.

Conclude all corrected Definition(i)–(iv) and Proposition(1)–(4) conditions, with closed maximal centers supplied by pair USC and branchwise regularity. The original obstruction is resolved by the corrected mathematically appropriate interface; do not claim standalone USC.

alternative_auxiliary_construction.assessment: No complete construction retaining both standalone auxiliary USC and all current branch formulas/center comparisons is established by the source or this audit. The exact existing formulas are conclusively incompatible with that stronger clause.
alternative_auxiliary_construction.nu_alone_possible: For a fixed finite resolution sequence, a different globally USC integer nu can be constructed backwards by nu_i(p)=1_{C_i}(p)+max({nu_{i+1}(q):q maps to p and remains in support} union {0}). Properness makes the fiber-maximum superlevels closed and adding the closed-center indicator preserves integer USC. This nu strictly drops above centers and is unchanged off them. This is an alternative future-dependent termination invariant, not the source nu, and does not repair rho.
alternative_auxiliary_construction.rho_difficulty: Changing rho to a primary-sensitive global envelope can alter its tie-breaking maxima inside a fixed primary stratum. Folding rho into primary inv can destroy the stated descent when inv stays equal and rho increases after a blowup; folding nu ahead of rho changes the monomial center priority. Constant rho would require replacing singular maximal-primary support loci with a different center-selecting primary invariant. Those are new constructions with additional proof and changed formula obligations.
alternative_auxiliary_construction.selection: Use the pair/stratum interface. This preserves all sound source functions and theorem conclusions with local proof and consumer corrections. This audit does not claim that every alternative stronger construction is impossible.
